reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited paragraphs (§ 3 use restrictions, § 20 general matters) contain no audit, inspection, verification or system-access right running against the Customer; absence of any audit obligation is more favorable than the playbook preferred position, so no edit is warranted.

Treating this as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct: the AUDIT rule exists to constrain a Vendor-favorable right, so its absence benefits our party and should not be raised as a negotiation issue.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is explained by the total absence of an audit clause and does not indicate a defect in the finding.
